headline: Africa's Solar Boom Outpaces Official Records
meta_description: Africa installed a record 17 GW of solar in 2026, but three-quarters remains invisible to official statistics because it's distributed solar.
summary_short: Africa hit a solar milestone in 2026 with 17 GW of new capacity—yet most of it flies under the radar because it's small-scale distributed power.
body:
Africa installed a record 17 gigawatts of solar capacity in 2026, yet official statistics barely register the achievement. The reason is simple: three-quarters of that growth came from distributed solar—small installations on rooftops and in communities—which traditional energy tracking systems struggle to capture.

This gap between installed reality and recorded data reveals a hidden energy revolution. Distributed solar works differently from large utility-scale farms. It's decentralized, often informal, and harder to quantify through conventional channels. Yet it reaches people and businesses the grid has always missed.

The numbers tell the real story: while policymakers and international agencies count only the visible megaprojects, millions of Africans are quietly powering homes and enterprises with their own solar systems. The continent's energy transformation is already underway—just not in the places official records are looking.
quick_facts: Africa installed 17 GW of solar capacity in 2026
Three-quarters of new solar is distributed, small-scale installations
Distributed solar remains largely invisible to official statistics
